question: Is the parastatal's territorial/geographic jurisdiction specifically defined in it's enabling law?
step2_answer: ANSWER: Not determined. Initially, 115 revenue villages of Bhubaneswar, Khordha and Jatni were taken into its jurisdiction, but due to bifurcation and inclusion of new villages, at present the number of villages under its jurisdiction stands at 556." It gives a table with a total BDA area of 1110.26 sq km across 556 villages. (2) The BDA Jurisdiction Map (BDA-06) lists revenue villages with areas and shows a 'B.D.A. Area Boundary'. It is a BDA-published map, and its title shows it covers villages 'proposed for extention'. (3) ODA (Planning and Building Standards) Rules, 2020 (BDA-08), rule 1(2): "They shall extend to all the 'development areas' which are so declared under sub-section (1) of Section 3 of the Odisha Development Authorities Act., 1982." This shows that areas are declared by notification under s.3(1) of the Act. (4) The Annual Report 2026 (BDA-03, p.23) says a proposal to extend the Act over 143 more villages under s.3(1) 'has been sent to Government for further notification'. This extension is not yet notified. | CAVEATS: The jurisdiction is set by Government notification under s.3(1). The sheet has neither the Act text nor the notification(s) fixing the current

ALL-01, ALL-02 and BDA-32 did not open, so a 0 was not available. A person should confirm against the s.3(1) notifications. The extension to 143 more villages (Annual Report 2026) is only proposed and is not counted.
